title: A project installation: the owned root in the project, referred to from omp's project plugin directory, writing no operator's own setting
situation: Decision 0312 kept a project installation's status-line choice in the project's settings. The architect has since generalized: every operator's own setting, a tier's model and how the session shows its agent alike, is written by no project installation, which is shared through the project.
decision: As 0312, with (5) restated. (1) install and uninstall take `--scope user|project`, user by default; on a terminal install asks for the scope it is not told, user preselected, wherever the project resolved from the working directory is not the home; `--yes` or no terminal takes user. (2) The project is the one omp anchors its plugins at from the working directory: the nearest ancestor holding `.omp/` other than the home, else the nearest holding `.git`, else the working directory; project scope is refused where that is the home. (3) A project's owned root is `<project>/.cratylus/<harness>`, laid out as the user's, and its installation record states its scope. (4) Its references are in `<project>/.omp/plugins`, each relative: a link `node_modules/cratylus-omp` to the root, a relative `file:` dependency entry in that directory's `package.json`, and one `.gitignore` block, owned by its exact content, re-including that link. (5) A project install neither asks for nor writes any operator's own setting, in the project or anywhere else: no model role and no status-line choice. `--model-roles` and `--agent-status` at project scope are each refused, naming the user scope. It reads, without writing, the project's and the user's settings, and names as the operator's next step, to settle at user scope, each tier neither binds and, where those settings hide the session's agent, showing it. (6) A project install or uninstall writes nothing under the home. (7) The version-skew warning and report name the scope and root, and the remedy names its scope. (8) The operator's command, with no installation named, reads the nearest project installation above the working directory, else the user's. (9) Install refuses a project root over an author's render tree, and `project` refuses to render over an installation. (10) A project uninstall also removes the project's `.omp/` directory where install created it and it is left empty.
consequences: One builder; review Ask. The command reference's status-line and project-scope text changes with it.
